question: In which language did the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius write the private notebook now called the Meditations?
answer: Greek. Educated Romans did philosophy in the language of Zeno and Chrysippus, and Marcus wrote his notes to himself in it, some on campaign along the Danube. The title Meditations is a later label; the manuscripts call the work To Himself. The ruler of the Latin-speaking empire addressed himself in Greek.
move: Ask what language a field thought in, not only where its thinkers lived.
trap: A Roman emperor, so Latin, the language of Roman law and army.
reference: Marcus Aurelius, Meditations, trans. Hard, ed. Gill, Oxford World's Classics, Oxford University Press, 2011
